sections.What the paper proposes: The paper (Frog in the Pan: Continuous Information and Momentum) proposes Information discreteness (ID): the sign of the formation-period cumulative return (PRET) times the percentage of formation-period days with negative daily returns minus the percentage with positive daily returns. Daily return signs are equally weighted, ignoring magnitude. Small (low) ID = continuous information; large (high) ID = discrete information. Stocks are first sorted on PRET, then on ID as the signal, sorted by quintiles, favoring the past winners (highest PRET quintile) in the lowest-ID (continuous information) subportfolio. Rationale: Frog-in-the-pan (limited attention): investors are inattentive to information arriving continuously in small amounts and process it with a delay, so momentum is stronger and more persistent after continuous information than after discrete information with similar cumulative formation-period returns.
sections.What we implemented and changed: We adapted 8 fields and assumed 3. Adapted: sort_rule (double sort per rule table; inner sort terciles with a 15-name floor); breakpoints (no exchange or size breakpoints in our universe; equal-count sorts of eligible names); weighting (policy: equal weight everywhere); disfavored_group (policy: long-only, no short leg); universe_and_filters (policy: our 415-name S&P 500 survivor universe); price_floor (paper excludes stocks priced below $5; NOT applied: the snapshot's prices are split-adjusted, not as-traded, so a dollar floor would drop the wrong names (e.g. NVDA 2017-18)); sample_period (policy: our snapshot sample); inner_sort (415-name universe: quintile-within-quintile leaves ~17 names, under the 20-name floor; terciles with a 15-name floor). Assumed: formation_window set to 12; min_history_days set to 252; min_formation_days set to 15. Portfolios were formed in 132 months with 25.1 names on average.
sections.What the backtest found: Over the sample the strategy returned 11.87% a year net of costs, against 12.71% for the equal-weight universe and 13.45% for SPY. Its Sharpe ratio was 0.58 against 0.65 for the equal-weight universe, and its maximum drawdown was -35.1%. The alpha t-statistic was -0.99; it is reported, not used as a gate. Robustness across costs, sub-periods and ranked groups gave a rho of 1.00.
sections.What the simulation and economics found: Across the simulated paths, incremental fee income versus the equal-weight universe fund had a median present value of -$496k, with a 5th to 95th percentile range of -$7.6M to $5.8M. The share of paths with positive NPV after research cost was 42.8%, and 49.3% once the historical excess return is removed. Break-even AUM is not defined; it is reported, not headlined.
